# Nehemiah Chapter 13 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 473r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/NEH_013_page_001.jpg

---

## Consensus Translation

**1** On that day they read from the book of Moses in the hearing of the people, and in it was found written that no Ammonite or Moabite should ever enter the assembly of God,

**2** because they did not meet the people of Israel with bread and water, but hired Balaam against them to curse them — yet our God turned the curse into a blessing.

**3** When they heard the law, they separated from Israel all those of foreign descent.

**4** Now before this, the priest Eliashib, who had been appointed over the chambers of the house of our God and was related to Tobiah,

**5** had prepared for him a large chamber where they had previously stored the grain offering, the frankincense, the vessels, and the tithes of grain, wine, and oil prescribed for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers, and the contributions for the priests.

**6** During all this I was not in Jerusalem, for in the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon I had gone to the king. After some time I asked leave of the king

**7** and came to Jerusalem. I then discovered the evil that Eliashib had done for Tobiah, preparing a chamber for him in the courts of the house of God.

**8** I was very angry, and I threw all of Tobiah's household goods out of the chamber.

**9** Then I gave orders, and they cleansed the chambers. I brought back the vessels of the house of God, with the grain offering and the frankincense.

**10** I also found out that the portions for the Levites had not been given to them, so that the Levites and the singers who performed the service had each fled to his own field.

**11** I confronted the officials and said, "Why is the house of God forsaken?" I gathered them together and restored them to their stations.

**12** Then all Judah brought the tithe of the grain, wine, and oil into the storehouses.

**13** I appointed as treasurers over the storehouses Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah of the Levites, with Hanan son of Zaccur son of Mattaniah to assist them, for they were considered trustworthy. Their duty was to distribute to their brothers.

**14** Remember me, O my God, for this, and do not wipe out my faithful deeds that I have done for the house of my God and for its services.

**15** In those days I saw people in Judah treading winepresses on the Sabbath, bringing in heaps of grain and loading them on donkeys, along with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of loads, which they brought into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day. I warned them against selling food on that day.

**16** Tyrians who lived in the city brought in fish and all kinds of merchandise and sold them on the Sabbath to the people of Judah, in Jerusalem itself.

**17** Then I confronted the nobles of Judah and said to them, "What is this evil thing you are doing, profaning the Sabbath day?

**18** Did not your fathers act in this way, and did not our God bring all this disaster on us and on this city? Now you are bringing more wrath on Israel by profaning the Sabbath."

**19** As soon as it began to grow dark at the gates of Jerusalem before the Sabbath, I commanded that the doors be shut and directed that they should not be opened until after the Sabbath. I stationed some of my servants at the gates so that no load could be brought in on the Sabbath day.

**20** Then the merchants and sellers of all kinds of merchandise camped outside Jerusalem once or twice.

**21** I warned them and said, "Why do you camp outside the wall? If you do so again, I will use force against you." From that time on they did not come on the Sabbath.

**22** I commanded the Levites to purify themselves and come and guard the gates, to keep the Sabbath day holy. Remember this also for me, O my God, and spare me according to the greatness of your steadfast love.

**23** In those days also I saw Jews who had married women of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

**24** Half of their children spoke the language of Ashdod, and none of them could speak the language of Judah, but only the language of each people.

**25** I confronted them and cursed them and struck some of them and pulled out their hair. I made them take an oath before God: "You shall not give your daughters to their sons, or take their daughters for your sons or for yourselves.

**26** Did not Solomon king of Israel sin on account of such women? Among the many nations there was no king like him, and he was beloved by his God, and God made him king over all Israel. Yet even him foreign women caused to sin.

**27** Shall we then listen to you and do all this great evil, acting treacherously against our God by marrying foreign women?"

**28** One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son-in-law to Sanballat the Horonite. I drove him away from me.

**29** Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and the Levites.

**30** Thus I cleansed them from everything foreign and established the duties of the priests and the Levites, each in his work,

**31** and provided for the wood offering at appointed times and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

---

## SOPHIA's Council Notes

Nehemiah 13 is one of the Hebrew Bible's most honest and troubling conclusions. After the triumphant wall dedication of chapter 12, Nehemiah returns from a trip to Persia to find nearly every covenant commitment from chapter 10 violated: the temple chambers have been given to Tobiah (the very enemy from ch. 2), the Levites' support has collapsed, the Sabbath is being profaned by commerce, and intermarriage has produced children who cannot even speak Hebrew. Nehemiah's forceful response — confrontation, expulsion, physical violence, and restructuring — reveals both his passionate faithfulness and the limits of human reform. The book ends not with resolution but with a prayer: "Remember me, O my God, for good." This open ending is theologically profound: the restoration of Israel remains incomplete, awaiting a faithfulness that no human leader can fully secure.

---

## Disagreement Log

### V.8 — "threw out" vs. "threw all of Tobiah's belongings out" vs. "I threw all the household goods outside"
- **EMET:** "I-threw all the-household-goods of-Toviyah outside" / **LOGOS:** "I threw all of Tobiah's household furnishings out" / **PNEUMA:** "I threw all of Tobiah's belongings out of the room"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "I threw all of Tobiah's household goods out of the chamber" — "Household goods" (*kelei beyt*) is more precise than "belongings" (too broad) or "furnishings" (too narrow). "Chamber" preserves the temple vocabulary.

### V.22 — "steadfast love" vs. "covenant-faithfulness" vs. "faithful love"
- **EMET:** "covenant-faithfulness" (*chasdekha*) / **LOGOS:** "steadfast love" / **PNEUMA:** "faithful love"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "steadfast love" — Consistent with project convention for *chesed*. In Nehemiah's personal prayer, the covenantal dimension is carried by the context.

### V.25 — "struck some and pulled out their hair" — degree of interpretation
- **EMET:** "struck some of-them men and-pulled-out-their-hair" / **LOGOS:** "struck some of them and pulled out their hair" / **PNEUMA:** "I struck some of them and pulled out their hair"
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "struck some of them and pulled out their hair" — All three agree on the basic rendering. The actions are reported without editorial softening or intensification. The Hebrew is direct and so should the translation be.

---

*— SOPHIA, in council with EMET, LOGOS, and PNEUMA*
